title: the Upper Fly River Rising
premise: Theo Brightwater, a disgraced railroad engineer drifting through the Upper Fly River country with a map of closed lines he shouldn't have, is hired to trace a vanished government survey team whose camp was found intact but empty. With a leaking boat, a monsoon bearing down, and a local guide named Kari who knows more about the missing team than she admits, Theo follows the closed lines into the highlands and discovers the surveyors were erased to bury evidence of a rigged land deal. When the monsoon makes landfall, Theo must choose between saving the proof and saving the people carrying it, and in doing so finally stops running and claims a name worth keeping.
about_author: Ada Thackeray is the pen name of a former hydrographic surveyor who spent six years charting river systems across Papua New Guinea before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels where landscapes are characters and survival is never free.

chapters.title: The Map That Wouldn't Burn
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Broke and drifting in Port Moresby, Theo takes a courier job upriver, hiding the map of closed rail lines he stole from his old firm. The emotional beat is restless guilt: he keeps moving because stopping means answering for what he did.

chapters.title: Gear Without Ghosts
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. At a river trading post, Theo finds the government survey team's camp: tents pitched, kettle warm, instruments laid out, no tracks leaving. A district officer offers him triple pay to follow the team's route. The beat is dread sharpening into temptation.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Oar
chapters.summary: Kari's POV. Kari, a guide whose brother was on the survey team, forces her way aboard Theo's leaking boat as payment for passage knowledge. She lies about why. The beat is wary alliance between two people both concealing something.

chapters.title: Closed Lines
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Following the old rail grades inland, Theo realizes the 'closed' lines were never abandoned—they were rerouted around land someone wanted hidden from official maps. First sign they're being followed. The beat is the thrill of competence curdling into fear.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: Kari's POV. They find the first surveyor alive but delirious, babbling about a ledger and men in company colors. Kari admits her brother carried it. The beat is grief breaking open trust; Theo chooses to keep going rather than turn back.

chapters.title: The Company's Men
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Ambushed at a trestle ruin, Theo and Kari escape downstream but lose most of their supplies as the sky turns monsoon-black. Theo recognizes the lead pursuer: his old supervisor. The beat is betrayal made personal—his past has caught him.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Kari's POV. The monsoon hits. Bailing water through the night, they shelter in a flooded cave where Kari reveals the full truth: the deal Theo's old firm signed erased three villages, including hers. The beat is fury and the collapse of Theo's last excuse that he didn't know.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. They reach the second surveyor, who hands over the ledger proving the land fraud, then dies of his wounds. Pursuers close in as floodwaters rise. Theo must choose: run with the proof alone or carry the injured Kari slower. He carries her. The beat is sacrifice over self-preservation.

chapters.title: High Water
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Climax: cornered on a collapsing rail bridge above the swollen river, Theo uses his engineer's knowledge to drop the span behind them, cutting off the pursuers at the cost of the only route out. The ledger survives lashed to his chest. The beat is terror transfigured into resolve.

chapters.title: The Name I Keep
chapters.summary: Kari's POV. After the storm breaks, they deliver the ledger to a magistrate downriver; the company's men are arrested, though the powerful escape punishment for now. Theo stays—first time in years—and begins surveying an honest line for Kari's people. The beat is quiet redemption: identity chosen, not fled.
